config_name: IdeaPad Slim 3i 15.6" — Core i5-1335U, 16GB LPDDR5, 512GB SSD, FHD, numeric keypad

specs.gpu: Intel Iris Xe Graphics (80 EU, integrated)
specs.keyboard_notes: Full-size with numeric keypad, bilingual CA

battery.notes: Capacity not published on BBY spec; 15.6" Slim 3i class uses ~50Wh. i5-1335U mid-load ~5-6h real.

offers.name: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i 15.6" FHD Laptop-Grey(Intel Core i5-1335U/16GB RAM/512GB SSD/Intel Iris Xe Graphics/Numeric Keypad/720p HD Camera/Win 11)

reviews.quote: It's one of the cheaper 15.6-inch laptops you can find without resorting to used systems; a decent barebones experience so long as you keep your expectations in check.
Not going to set anyone's world on fire, but a great value for those that just need a Windows computer.
Sits just a rung or two above the minimum viable Windows laptop, held back by lackluster battery life and a limited raw-performance ceiling.

praises: 16GB LPDDR5 standard — the only 3i at BBY that won't choke on 30 Chrome tabs
Numeric keypad on a 1.65 kg 15.6" chassis is a real productivity plus for spreadsheets
i5-1335U with Iris Xe handles light video editing and older games far better than UHD-graphics siblings
Iris Xe drives two external 4K monitors via HDMI+DP-over-USB-C without complaint
Sturdy for the price; the 15.6" shell feels less flexy than the 15.3" models
complaints: Panel type unstated and buyers report the dull TN variant: poor viewing angles and washed colour
Regular $1,279.99 is overpriced for a budget TN panel; only the sale price is defensible
720p webcam is the weakest camera of any current 3i SKU
LPDDR5 is soldered — 16GB is fixed, no upgrade path
Fan spins up audibly during Teams calls with camera on

standouts: Best raw x86 CPU+iGPU combo of the IdeaPad budget line — Iris Xe and 16GB make it the closest thing to a real work machine here
design_philosophy: The upper tier of the IdeaPad Slim 3 family: a 15.6" shell with numeric keypad and a 13th-gen Core i5 with Iris Xe and 16GB soldered LPDDR5, aimed at buyers who need real multitasking headroom but not a Slim 5 price. Panel and webcam are where Lenovo pays for that CPU.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-ideapad-slim3.md). Inferred from Core 5 320 sibling anchoring: +1.3 productivity (10-core + 16GB + numpad), +1.0 gaming (Iris Xe vs UHD), −0.3 battery (hotter 13th-gen U at 15.6"), screen_quality −0.5 for likely TN panel (BBY does not state IPS; BUDGET_LIST rule = assume TN).
